model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between co-occurrence number (x-axis) and classification accuracy (ACC, y-axis in %) for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” spans from 0 to approximately 10⁴ using a logarithmic scale, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, ranges from 35% to 65% with linear scaling and tick marks at 5% intervals. The “Base” method (black line with circular markers) remains relatively flat, starting near 38% and rising slightly to ~44%. “FT” (light blue line with downward triangles) begins at ~40% and increases steadily to ~48%. “IKE” (red line with upward triangles) starts at ~43% and rises to ~49.5%. “MEND” (brown line with diamond markers) begins at ~44% and climbs to ~56.5%. “MEMIT” (purple line with pentagon markers) starts at ~44% and increases to ~55%. “ROME” (green line with square markers) exhibits the steepest growth, starting at ~51% and rising to ~66.5% as co-occurrence number increases. All methods show a general upward trend in accuracy with higher co-occurrence numbers, though their rates of improvement vary significantly.
